limit: The feasible point is borderline: fb_loss_frac=0.099905 is only 0.000095 below 0.1, within the 1% tolerance, and p=0.186 L=1000 is infeasible at 0.101361; the interval 0.185<p<0.186 was not tested. The fa gain from p=0.185 to p=0.186 is only 0.374%, inside tolerance, so a finer p is unlikely to change the recommendation, but a safety-margin choice would be p=0.18 L=1000. Evidence: E4, E5, C5, V5.
explanation: lc is saturated, and the scheduler gives fa the normalized part p/(p+0.5) and fb 0.5/(p+0.5), using work-conserving unused capacity when fb is not backlogged. fa_goodput_bps rises with p while fb_loss_frac rises once fb's weighted service falls below its 80 Mbps offer. lc.queue.length=1000 does not change steady-state delivered goodputs but lowers measured fb_loss_frac by leaving more packets queued at the measurement boundary. This makes p=0.185 L=1000 feasible, while p=0.186 L=1000 exceeds the loss limit. At this setting fa has enough backlog that fa.type does not change the goal metrics; TcpBbr gives the same measured fa_goodput_bps and fb_loss_frac as TcpCubic.

claims.text: fa_goodput_bps is governed by lc scheduler service and work-conserving unused capacity, not by TCP congestion control when fa has backlog.
The fb_loss_frac <=0.1 constraint binds the optimum: p=0.185 L=1000 is feasible at 0.099905, while p=0.186 L=1000 is infeasible at 0.101361.
lc.queue.length=1000 lowers measured fb_loss_frac without changing delivered goodput by increasing end-of-window queue backlog.
At p=0.185 L=1000, TcpCubic and TcpBbr give identical goal metrics: fa_goodput_bps=26036198 and fb_loss_frac=0.099905.
The best tested feasible fa_goodput_bps is 26036198 at p=0.185 L=1000; p=0.186 L=1000 gives only 26133504, a 0.374% gain inside tolerance, but violates the loss condition.

open_questions: F11: The la_util difference between TcpCubic and TcpBbr at p=0.185 L=1000 is plausibly due Cubic's growing fa queue, but the queue-growth test was ruled inconclusive.
F12: q_fa_first=133 in E7 versus lc_q_fa=121 at t=2.000 in T11 remains unresolved; it may be a sampling-boundary convention.
F13: TcpBbr's q_fa_first=7 and q_fa_last=6 with la_util=0.027007 is not explained by a fair test.
